edges.subject: MFSD8
edges.quote: Defects in the MFSD8 gene encoding the lysosomal membrane protein CLN7 lead to CLN7 disease, a neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disorder belonging to the group of neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses.

edges.subject: CLN5
edges.object: reduced protein levels in Cln7 knockout lysosomes
edges.quote: One of the most significantly depleted lysosomal proteins was Cln5 protein that underlies another distinct neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis disorder.

edges.subject: CLN7
edges.object: proteolytic degradation of CLN5 protein by cysteine proteases
edges.quote: the depletion of mature Cln5 protein was due to increased proteolytic degradation by cysteine proteases in Cln7 ko lysosomes.

edges.subject: CLN7 disease
edges.quote: depletion of multiple soluble lysosomal proteins suggest a critical role of CLN7 for lysosomal function, which may contribute to the pathogenesis and progression of CLN7 disease.

edges.subject: CLN7 disease
edges.object: impaired mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 reactivation
edges.quote: we found a defect in the ability of Cln7 ko MEFs to adapt to starvation conditions as shown by impaired mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 reactivation, reduced autolysosome tubulation and increased perinuclear accumulation of autolysosomes compared with controls.
